problems.title: Averaged prototypes require a separate history condition
claim: The local trimming proposition reasons about the current boundary \(q\); deployment can instead use an averaged boundary \(\bar q\).
analysis: With \(q=(1,10,1)\), prior removed direction \((0,1,1)/\sqrt2\), current removed direction \(e_2\), and current feature \((1,-1,1)\), the local corrected margin is \(2\). The history-averaged boundary \((1,2.25,-1.75)\) instead gives margin \(-0.75\). The local conditions hold, but averaging adds an uncontrolled term.

For the deployed history rule, the signed margin is \(m_{\rm local}+y\hat z^\top(\bar q-q)\). The additional condition \(|\hat z^\top(\bar q-q)|<m_{\rm local}\) suffices for a positive margin. This explains the local theorem’s coverage; it does not amend a disproved theorem.
result: The local proposition survives; it does not alone guarantee the deployed history rule.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an explicit scope clarification rather than a supported error in the local theorem.
problems.existing_correction_status: Scope clarification only; no author-paper repair or adoption is asserted.

problems.title: Removing beyond positive rank can erase an arbitrary null direction
problems.source_location: Sections 4.1–4.2, p. 4, Eq. (1); Section 6, p. 7; methods/tact_utils.py lines 214–217.
claim: The method removes the leading \(m\) covariance eigenvectors as augmentation-varying directions.
analysis: For covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(0,2,0)\), only \(e_2\) varies. Removing two directions permits ordered bases \((e_2,e_1,e_3)\) or \((e_2,e_3,e_1)\), which respectively erase or preserve causal feature \(e_1\). Nullspace choices do not encode observed augmentation variation.
result: The removal count needs a rank convention. This does not prove that published selected settings encounter the ambiguity or that all positive-variance directions are noncausal.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Cap removal by a declared numerical positive-rank threshold. If a positive-eigenvalue tie is split, specify a subspace-level or invariant tie convention.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a rank boundary in a proxy operation, with no demonstrated central experimental damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
